Na Bíblia, pastorear é uma imagem de lid: In the Bible, shepherding is an image of leadership. Abel, Abraham, Moses and David tended sheep before they cared for people, and Israel's kings were called to be shepherds of the people.

Agostinho dizia que o coração humano viv: Augustine said that the human heart is restless until it rests in God. Psalm 23 is that restlessness finding its place: not the absence of valleys, but the certainty of a Presence. Perhaps today's question is not “where am I going?” but “who is leading me?”
Logo depois da primeira desobediência, n: Right after the first disobedience in Eden, it is God who goes searching: “Where are you?” From the very beginning, the initiative of reconciliation is his, not ours.

Pensadores cristãos sempre perceberam qu: Christian thinkers have always seen that the greatest obstacle to receiving this love is not our wickedness but our pride: it is hard to accept a gift we cannot pay for. Perhaps faith begins exactly there, on the day we stop bargaining with God and simply let ourselves be loved.
Em Gênesis, o ser humano é colocado no j: In Genesis, human beings are placed in the garden “to work it and keep it.” We were created to work with God, reflecting his care over the world.
Efésios 2 inverte essa lógica. A salvaçã: Ephesians 2 turns that logic around. Salvation is charis, grace: a gift that cannot be bought. No one can boast, because no one contributed anything.
Mas Paulo continua: somos “feitura” de D: But Paul continues: we are God's “workmanship,” in Greek poiēma, a word linked to a carefully crafted work. In Christ, God begins creation again, now in us.
Abraham Kuyper lembrava que não existe u: Abraham Kuyper reminded us that there is not a square inch of life that Christ does not claim as his own. The question is no longer “what must I do to be accepted?” but “what can I do, already accepted?”

O jugo era a peça que unia dois bois par: The yoke was the piece that joined two oxen so they could pull together. The image is not of the absence of work but of walking harnessed to someone gentle and humble, who carries the weight with us.
Vivemos numa cultura que mede valor por: We live in a culture that measures worth by productivity. Even rest has become a strategy to get more done. Jesus offers another kind of rest: the rest of someone who doesn't need to justify themselves by what they produce.
Pascal observou que boa parte da infelic: Pascal observed that much human unhappiness comes from not knowing how to sit quietly in a room. True rest may not be the absence of tasks but the presence of meaning.

Bem no centro do livro, o poeta se lembr: Right at the center of the book, the poet remembers something and hope returns. The Hebrew word hesed describes the loyal love of the covenant, the love that remains when everything falls.
Em Jesus vemos o hesed de Deus em carne:: In Jesus we see God's hesed in the flesh: faithful all the way to the cross. That is why we can lament honestly and, in the same breath, say: “The Lord is my portion.”
A fé bíblica não pede que finjamos que e: Biblical faith does not ask us to pretend everything is fine. It teaches us to weep and to hope at the same time, without one canceling the other.
Paulo conhecia esse padrão, mas precisou: Paul knew this pattern, but he had to live it in his own body. Three times he asked for a “thorn in the flesh” to be taken away, and the answer was not healing but presence: “My grace is sufficient for you.”
No centro dessa história está a cruz. Em: At the center of this story stands the cross. In 1 Corinthians, Paul says that the message of a crucified Messiah looks like foolishness and weakness, but it is the power of God for salvation.
Nossa cultura esconde fragilidades e cel: Our culture hides frailty and celebrates those who never fall. The gospel, by contrast, lets us be honest about our limits, because the center of the story is not our strength.
Kierkegaard dizia que a fé exige uma esp: Kierkegaard said that faith requires a kind of surrender: ceasing to be our own foundation. O verbo “lançar” (epiriptō) é o mesmo us: The verb “cast” (epiriptō) is the same one used when the disciples threw their cloaks on Jesus' colt (Luke 19). It is a concrete gesture of transferring the weight.
Pedro sabia o que era ansiedade: afundou: Peter knew what anxiety was: he sank when he looked at the wind and denied Jesus out of fear. And he was restored by a Lord who cared for him when he failed.
Há um paradoxo bonito aqui: a humildade: There is a beautiful paradox here: humility sets us free. A ressurreição de Jesus, no primeiro dia: Jesus' resurrection, on the first day of the week, is the beginning of that new creation. That is why Paul says: if anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation.
Junto vem a reconciliação. O verbo grego: Reconciliation comes with it. The Greek verb katallassō speaks of exchanging hostility for peace. God reconciles the world to himself and entrusts that ministry to the reconciled.
Isso significa que ninguém está preso pa: This means no one is trapped forever in what has been. In Christ, a new beginning is not a self-help effort; it is a creative act of God.
Davi não diz apenas que o Senhor é um pa: David does not just say that the Lord is a shepherd, but that he is “my” shepherd. Peça a Deus discernimento para enxergar: Ask God for discernment to see a good work prepared for you today: a visit, a phone call, a quiet act of service.

Identifique uma limitação que costuma en: Identify a limitation that usually embarrasses you and hand it to God in prayer, asking that it become a place of dependence.
Pedro liga humildade e entrega: humilhar: Peter links humility and surrender: humbling ourselves under God's hand includes admitting that we don't control everything. We cast our anxiety on him because he cares for us, not because the problem is small.
Faça uma lista do que está ansiando você: Make a list of what is making you anxious and pray through it item by item. If the anxiety persists, also talk to someone you trust or a professional.
